rationale: C01 plausibly supplied a material template for the child's specialized Selective Service program. Both establish a separate regulatory part for a defined class of registrants and use substantially the same administrative machinery: local-board processing, classification, Armed Forces physical examination, review or appeal, selection for service, notification, and subsequent reclassification. C11 and C20 contain narrower analogues involving registrant-initiated requests and special processing, but neither matches the child's overall sequence as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: If the registrant has been or is found to be acceptable for service in the Armed Forces after an armed forces physical examination, the local board shall refer the registrant's request...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The physical examination of a special registrant shall be accomplished in the manner provided in Part 1628... [and] the State Director of Selective Service shall maintain a record... of each special registrant who has been found acceptable for service in the armed forces.
shared_material.explanation: Both make Armed Forces physical acceptability a formal prerequisite within a special registrant-processing track administered through local and state Selective Service authorities.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The same persons who are authorized under the provisions of Part 1626 or Part 1627... may, in like manner, appeal... Such appeals shall be taken and processed in the same manner...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: A special registrant shall be entitled to the same rights of appearance before a local board, reopening of classification, appeal to the appeal board, and appeal to the President, as provided in Parts 1624, 1625, 1626, and 1627...
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts C01's technique of incorporating the ordinary Selective Service appeal system into a specialized regulatory program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Upon being notified that the registrant has enlisted in a unit of the Ready Reserve, the local board shall reopen his classification and classify him anew.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each special registrant who has not attained the fifty-first anniversary... shall be considered by the local board as available for military service and eligible for classification in Class I-A...
shared_material.explanation: The child uses the same classification-centered local-board machinery, modifying the consequence to reopening and reclassification after Ready Reserve enlistment.

shared_material.child_excerpt: PART 1680—SELECTION OF CERTAIN PERSONS WHO HAVE CRITICAL SKILLS FOR ENLISTMENT IN UNITS OF THE READY RESERVE
shared_material.parent_excerpt: PART 1650 - REGISTRATION, CLASSIFICATION, PHYSICAL EXAMINATION, SELECTION, AND INDUCTION OF PERSONS IN MEDICAL, DENTAL, AND ALLIED SPECIALIST CATEGORIES
shared_material.explanation: Both are stand-alone regulatory parts governing the selection and military processing of registrants with specified professional or critical skills.
